basis: BWS-like imprinting disorder with hyperinsulinism and lateralized overgrowth; macroglossia is variable, without established common gastrointestinal impairment.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: macroglossia is variable; neither a defining gastrointestinal abnormality nor common functional damage is established for this mosaic disorder.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: lateralized somatic and skeletal overgrowth is a characteristic component of the BWS-like phenotype.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia; cardiac abnormalities and vesicoureteral reflux each occur in 1/1 assessed, and microtia in 2/2. Very small denominators limit frequency estimates.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: ventricular septal defect and tricuspid regurgitation each occur in 1/1 assessed; these are structural or functional cardiac abnormalities.
decisions.renal: involved: vesicoureteral reflux in 1/1 assessed establishes urinary tract dysfunction, although the denominator is very small.
decisions.otologic: involved: microtia in 2/2 assessed represents structural underdevelopment of the external ear.

basis: Peroxisome biogenesis disorder; neurologic and damaging ocular disease affect most. Rhizomelic forms predominate (>50%) and cause skeletal dysplasia; Refsum forms lack this feature.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: rhizomelic chondrodysplasia predominates among these PEX5/PEX7 disorders, making skeletal involvement common overall despite its absence in Refsum disease.

basis: Defined by acrofacial dysostosis with dental and ectodermal abnormalities. Oligodontia occurs in 80-99%, sparse hair in 30-79%; cutis aplasia and pili torti are occasional.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: oligodontia is explicitly part of the syndrome definition and occurs in 80-99%; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: the definition includes cutis aplasia and hair abnormalities; frequent sparse hair supports the defining ectodermal phenotype.

basis: Universal neurodevelopmental impairment with progressive spasticity. Constipation (9/16) and reflux (8/16) do not establish direct gastrointestinal damage; neonatal hypoglycemia is transient.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: constipation (9/16) and reflux (8/16) are common, but the record does not establish intrinsic gastrointestinal damage or disease-specific loss of gut function.

basis: A cutaneous vascular lesion defined by superficial dermal capillary ectasia and overlying epidermal hyperkeratosis.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: ectasia of dermal capillaries defines the lesion; capillaries explicitly fall within the cardiovascular axis.

basis: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy. Amyotrophy in 2/2 does not establish direct muscle disease rather than secondary wasting from severe neurologic disability.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: generalized amyotrophy (2/2) establishes wasting, but direct muscle pathology is not demonstrated; secondary wasting does not meet the direct-damage rule.

basis: ATP synthase deficiency with intellectual disability and neuropathy in most reported cases. Cardiomyopathy is listed without a frequency establishing common involvement.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: hypertrophic cardiomyopathy has no supplied frequency, and common involvement (>=30%) or a major cardiac diagnostic criterion is not established.

basis: Axonal neuropathy with persistent vocal cord paresis in 8/8, causing laryngeal dysfunction; structural foot deformity, pes cavus, occurs in 6/8.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: pes cavus in 6/8 (75%) is an established structural locomotor deformity, beyond weakness or hypotonia alone.

basis: Autoinflammatory immunodeficiency with amylopectin storage; damaging skeletal myopathy affects most classic cases, and cardiomyopathy roughly a third or more of reported patients.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: myocardial amylopectin accumulation causes cardiomyopathy in roughly >=30% of classic reported cases; this is direct storage-related damage.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: skeletal muscle amylopectinosis with myopathy is characteristic and affects most classic reported cases, rather than being incidental storage.
